channel.title: Sun Prairie ALPR news and updates
channel.description: An independent, unofficial community project about the Sun Prairie, WI Police Department’s license plate reader program. Not affiliated with the City of Sun Prairie or SPPD. Summaries were drafted with AI help.

item.title: Archive updated to the Complete Edition (344 pages)
item.description: The archive is now version 3.0 with a new contents list, a 165-page ALPR-only volume, a new summary and overview, and a press kit.

item.title: Chief open to a quarterly ALPR transparency report
item.description: Chief Warych replied that he is open to a report like the one-page outline sent to him, needs to confirm the numbers are available, and will look at it after approval during onboarding. Not a commitment.

item.title: Taylor, Texas ends its Flock contract
item.description: The city cited low use, no clear help solving crimes, and data security concerns. Cameras disabled.

item.title: Oakland County, Michigan: parks drop Flock plate readers
item.description: Parks will let Flock plate reader subscriptions lapse; the Sheriff will not pursue a Flock drone contract.

item.title: York, Maine voters approve a ban on license plate readers
item.description: A ballot question asked whether to ban automatic license plate readers, including Flock’s. Voters approved it. The town must remove or shut off its Flock cameras and end the contract. Police said the cameras helped in investigations; residents raised privacy concerns. The article does not give the vote count.

item.title: Site update, Nov. 4, 2026
item.description: Added a Quiz tab, a working FAQ tab (the old FAQ link went to the Home page), a side-by-side comparison with Cedar Rapids, Henrico and Bloomington, a retention comparison, a table of what the Chief said versus what is written down, Myth or fact, a 2-minute comment, questions for your alder, a printable flyer with a QR code, a press kit, hashtags, news search and sorting, a list of places that ended plate readers, a calendar file, an RSS feed, a privacy note, theme and text-size controls, and a back-to-top button.

item.title: Site update, Nov. 4, 2026
item.description: New News tab with recent stories about plate readers, Flock and Axon, with filters by topic. Each summary links to its source.

item.title: Henrico County, Virginia removes more than 120 Flock cameras itself
item.description: The county ended its contract over data-collection, data-access and privacy concerns. Flock was given until Oct. 21 to remove the cameras and did not, so county crews took them down on Oct. 31. Flock says it would have complied and is now coordinating the rest of the removal. The county has not announced a replacement.

item.title: Cedar Rapids police start using Axon plate readers, phasing out 70+ Flock cameras
item.description: The city says it will not add cameras, though locations may change. The 164-page contract budgets for 20 Axon Outpost cameras. Data is kept 30 days unless tied to an active investigation. The article cites a $14 million Axon agreement announced in August and a $14.6 million, decade-long public safety investment the council approved in June.

item.title: Site update, Oct. 31, 2026
item.description: New look for the Home page using the SP-ALPR logo: a logo header, key-number strip, a countdown to the Nov. 17 budget approval, Start here cards, and a What's new feed. The logo is also the app icon, the share image and the footer mark. Added a note to the report about the Chief's Oct. 27 answers.

item.title: Site update, Oct. 31, 2026
item.description: Replaced the advocacy archive with the newest version (264 pages, updated Oct. 31). It is shorter and reorganized: the contents list was rebuilt, the Student Voice material was regrouped, and it adds an at-a-glance summary, a glossary and a “What Changed in Each Update” page at the end.

item.title: League City, Texas puts Flock on the ballot (Proposition A)
item.description: The question was non-binding, but the council adopted a resolution to act on the result. The mayor said the cameras would be covered or disabled within 72 hours of certification if voters said no. The city manages 55 Flock cameras and keeps data 30 days. The vote was Nov. 3. A Houston Public Media headline says voters rejected the cameras, but I could not open that article, so check the result at the source.

item.title: Bloomington, Indiana council unanimously bans plate readers and shared third-party cameras
item.description: The ordinance goes to the mayor; a two-thirds council vote could override a veto. Closed-circuit park cameras and police body cameras are exempt. The sponsor pointed to concerns about federal immigration enforcement. The city’s 11 plate-reader cameras were already removed, and local police said Flock cameras helped solve crimes.

item.title: Flock lobbying and Wisconsin: who has cancelled, and who has not
item.description: Flock spent about $102,000 in 2025 lobbying for two Wisconsin bills (AB 300 and SB 299) that would have given grants for local plate readers; neither passed. The article lists Kaukauna, Sturgeon Bay, Verona, Appleton, Oshkosh, Dane County and Stoughton as having cancelled. Milwaukee kept its contract, and 12 of 15 council members asked for a review.

item.title: Cities are dropping Flock and switching to Axon plate readers
item.description: Reports that a handful of cities have replaced Flock with comparable Axon systems, including streetlamp-mounted cameras and in-car plate readers. The framing is that cities are changing vendors, not leaving plate readers. Most of the article is paywalled, so I am only summarizing the visible part. This is the same kind of switch the city is considering in Sun Prairie.

item.title: Sun Prairie PD’s plate readers concern some residents
item.description: Earlier local coverage. Police use plate readers on patrol vehicles and had recently started mounting them on utility poles. The Assistant Chief called them a “force multiplier.” A resident worried that anyone can request plate images through open records. Data is kept 30 days, and the city may budget for three more cameras. This is older than the rest of this page, so the camera counts may have changed.
